title: quant-kernel: improve INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion paths and KV-cache aware batching
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Improve throughput and tail latency for quantized inference (INT8/FP8) on common decoder-only LMs while preserving output quality. This PR implements a set of targeted kernel optimizations and control-plane changes: 1) a fused dequantization path that merges per-block dequant + matmul to avoid an intermediate full-precision activation copy, 2) an improved SmoothQuant scaling pass for INT8/FP8 that reduces quantization noise for attention projection layers, 3) KV-cache-aware continuous batching so that requests with warm KV cache are prioritized for faster response and grouped with compatible sequence-length distributions, and 4) scheduler hints to select the fused kernels when model and hardware profiles match. Changes are backward-compatible and gated by a runtime flag (quant::enable_fused_dequant) and model-compatibility table. Checklist: - [x] implement fused dequant + matmul kernels (CUDA + CPU fallback) - [x] integrate SmoothQuant tuning into quantization pipeline - [x] add scheduling hints for fused-path selection - [x] KV-cache-aware batching policy and tests - [x] benchmarks across 7B/13B model profiles - [x] add regression evals to ensure output parity within tolerance - [x] docs + release notes Context: This builds on the 2025 quant effort (previous PRs improving INT8 kernels) but focuses on end-to-end serving improvements when KV caching and continuous batching are active in production. The fused path reduces device memory traffic and removes an extra write-read of activations which was the main throughput bottleneck for large-batch INT8 runs. Performance: - Throughput: +1.6x median for LLaMA-2-7B INT8 on A10G under typical PLT (prompt length) distributions. - Tail latency (p95): -18% for interactive settings when fused path selected. - Token generation CPU overhead: -22% due to fewer host-device synchronizations. - Model quality: token-level KL and top-k agreement retained within 0.5% on our eval suites. Rollout: feature gated, default off for new deployments until canary completes. A canary rollout plan is attached in release_notes. Repro instructions and perf harness commands are in the commits.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you add microbenchmarks showing the memory bandwidth reduction and a breakdown of time spent in dequant vs matmul? Also please make CPU fallback explicit in the header.
Aisha Patel: Added microbenchmarks and included a CPU fallback implementation (see fused_dequant_matmul.cpp). Benchmarks attached to perf harness commit.
Rina Kawaguchi: Safety question — how do we ensure numeric stability of SmoothQuant in FP8 path? Please run the regression eval suite across a few seeds.

Ethan Brooks: CI failed on first run (perf-canary flaky). Reran workflow and fixed a race in the batcher that caused a rare double-enqueue; added a mutex and a test.
Miguel Santos: Approve after addressing microbench and adding the runtime flag.
Rina Kawaguchi: Approve — small nits addressed in separate follow-up PR.
release_notes: Improved quantized inference kernels: fused dequant+matmul path, SmoothQuant improvements for INT8/FP8, and KV-cache-aware continuous batching. Expected improvement: ~1.6x throughput for common 7B INT8 workloads and reduced p95 latency. Feature gated behind quant::enable_fused_dequant; canary rollout recommended.
notes_for_ops: Gate is off by default. To enable in a cluster: set runtime.config.quant.enable_fused_dequant=true and ensure node GPU profiles are present in runtime/config/gpu_profiles. Monitor metrics: quant.fused_path.hit_rate, batching.kv_warm_ratio, kernel_selector.fallback_rate. Canary on a small percentage of requests and watch token error rates.
